KisahKami.subtitle: “A village is shaped not only by time, but by the people who have cared for it.”
KisahKami.state1Text: The history of Grogol takes us back to a time when village governance in the Yogyakarta region was being formally organized. Within the history of the Sultanate of Yogyakarta, Rijksblad No. 12 of 1916 marked an important milestone.
KisahKami.state2Text: Several years later, through Rijksblad van Jogjakarta No. 10 of 1927, Grogol was recorded as one of 14 kalurahan in the Paliyan administrative district. In the historical records of Grogol, May 17, 1916 is recognized as the founding date.
KisahKami.state3Text: Yet Grogol's history does not always come to us through complete records. Some early government archives were lost, including documents destroyed when the house that also served as the office of Lurah Arjo Sukarso was burned down.
KisahKami.state4Text: He was followed by Lurah Sastro Diwirjo, who served from 1947 to 1965, guiding Grogol through the early years of Indonesia's independence.
KisahKami.state5Text: In 1965, Lurah Hadi Suwarno began a three-decade period of leadership that lasted until 1996. During his tenure, physical development in Grogol expanded significantly.
KisahKami.mosqueText: During this period, Ki Ageng Pemanahan Mosque was also established and later became one of Grogol's landmarks.
KisahKami.state6Text: After three decades under Hadi Suwarno, Lurah Sugiyarto led Grogol from 1996 to 2014. His tenure saw improvements to neighborhood roads and agricultural access roads, and the development of community activities.
KisahKami.state8Text: In 2021, the leadership baton was passed to Lurah Latip Wahyudi. From one generation to the next, Grogol's leadership has changed, but one thing has remained constant: the village continues to grow together with its people.
KisahKami.outroQuote: “Grogol's history is not something that has ended.”
KisahKami.outroText: It lives on in the memories of its elders, in the stories shared by its people, in its traditions, in the spaces of the village, and in the everyday lives of its community. And when you visit Grogol today, you are walking on land that has carried more than a century of stories.

KehidupanMasyarakat.title: Life in Grogol
KehidupanMasyarakat.subtitle: Where Local Life Becomes Part of the Journey
KehidupanMasyarakat.p1: Grogol is more than just a place in Gunungkidul. It is home to thousands of people whose lives are shaped by the land, traditions, creativity, and a strong sense of community.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p2: In 2024, Grogol was home to 2,421 people—1,170 men and 1,251 women—living in 910 households. The community is spread across six padukuhan, six RW, and 23 RT within an area of 4.59 km². With more than 1,500 residents of productive age, Grogol has a strong human resource base that plays an important role in the development of the kalurahan.
KehidupanMasyarakat.h1: A Community That Continues to Grow
KehidupanMasyarakat.p3: Life in Grogol reflects a blend of rural traditions and a growing modern community. The educational backgrounds of its residents are increasingly diverse. In 2024, 621 residents had completed senior high school, while 63 held diploma qualifications, 114 were university graduates, and 10 had completed master's or doctoral degrees. This diversity provides an important foundation for the community to develop social, economic, cultural, and tourism activities.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p4: Grogol also achieved a Village Development Index (IDM) score of 0.8221 in 2024. This status reflects the capacity of the community and the kalurahan government to foster social and economic development while promoting environmental sustainability.
KehidupanMasyarakat.h2: Farming, Caring for the Land, Sustaining Life
KehidupanMasyarakat.p5: Agriculture remains an important part of life in Grogol. Of its 4.59 km² area, approximately 356 hectares are rice fields. Most are rain-fed, while the remainder are supported by simple irrigation systems. This agricultural landscape reflects the community's close relationship with nature, the seasons, and the cycles of farming.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p6: For Grogol, agriculture is about more than producing food. It is also part of local knowledge and everyday life—a way of living that shapes the relationship between people, the land, and the environment.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p7: One of Grogol's greatest strengths lies in its culture. Traditions are not simply preserved as a legacy of the past; they continue to thrive through community-based arts groups.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p8: BPS data for 2024 records five gejog lesung groups, one karawitan group, one macapat group, one toklek/thek-thek group, and one Reog dance group in Grogol. There is also a ketoprak group and traditional wedding makeup studios that form part of the community's cultural life.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p9: This is where Grogol's culture finds its meaning. The sound of the wooden mortars, the music of gamelan, traditional dance movements, and community performances are more than spectacles. They grow from within the community and form part of the social spaces where people gather, learn, practice, and pass knowledge on to the next generation.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p10: Culture in Grogol also creates a space for generations to meet. Children learn about traditional arts from their surroundings, while older generations safeguard the knowledge and traditions passed down through time.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p11: So when visitors join a Reog workshop, try playing the gejog lesung, learn traditional dance, or experience a karawitan performance, they are not simply learning an art form. They are meeting the people who keep that knowledge alive.
KehidupanMasyarakat.h5: From Local Potential to Meaningful Experiences
KehidupanMasyarakat.p12: The development of Grogol as a tourism destination creates opportunities for the community to turn local potential into meaningful experiences as well as economic opportunities.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p13: Agriculture, traditional arts, culinary heritage, local creativity, and everyday life can all become part of the visitor experience. Guests can come not simply to see a place, but to interact with the people who call it home.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p14: This is the spirit of Grogol Kaloka: creating tourism rooted in local life.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p15: In Grogol, visitors can discover experiences that are closer and more personal—meeting local artists, learning from residents, tasting local food, discovering agricultural life, or simply sharing stories in the warmth of a rural community.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p16: Ultimately, Grogol's richness lies not only in its landscapes or tourism attractions.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p17: Grogol's greatest treasure is its people.
KehidupanMasyarakat.l1: The people who cultivate the land.
KehidupanMasyarakat.l2: The people who play the gamelan.
KehidupanMasyarakat.l3: The people who strike the wooden mortars.
KehidupanMasyarakat.l4: The people who teach traditional dance to children.
KehidupanMasyarakat.l5: The people who keep traditions alive.
KehidupanMasyarakat.l6: And the people who open their homes and cultural spaces to visitors.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p18: Coming to Grogol means coming to experience a living community—a community that continues to grow, evolve, and pass its heritage forward.
KehidupanMasyarakat.p19: Come to Grogol not only to see a destination, but to meet the people who bring it to life.
